$comment: Supported Question & Use-Case Catalog — machine-readable source of truth.
Derived on 2026-08-20 by inspecting the LIVE PostgreSQL database, the LIVE
Qdrant collection, the two MCP servers over the wire, and the agent code —
not from imagination. `data_facts` below is re-checked against PostgreSQL
and Qdrant by tests/use_cases/test_question_catalog.py, so a catalog that
drifts from the data fails rather than misleads.
`supported` is about the AGENT path (POST /chat), not about what SQL could
in principle answer. Data can exist in PostgreSQL, be exposed by MCP, and
still be unreachable through the agents — that gap is the point of this
document, and it is recorded rather than smoothed over.

data_facts.$comment: Asserted against the live stores by test_data_facts_still_match_the_database.

known_defects.title: The tool catalogue advertises four data tools that cannot be dispatched as a calculation
known_defects.detail: McpAgent.catalogue() lists get_yield_curve, get_rate_history, get_curve_slope and list_series as ToolSpecs. The domain expert may legitimately name any catalogue tool as `calculation`, but McpAgent._calculate dispatches only to RiskWorkflows methods, which are price_portfolio, compute_dv01, compute_var and run_stress. Naming get_curve_slope — the natural choice for a 2s10s question — returns {'error': "no workflow named 'get_curve_slope'"} instead of a slope.
known_defects.fix: ToolSpec gained `executable`. The four retrieval helpers are now advertised as informational; only the four risk workflows are schedulable, and DomainExpertAgent._build drops a calculation that is not on catalogue.executable_tools. Enforced by test_every_executable_capability_can_actually_be_dispatched and test_the_expert_cannot_schedule_an_informational_capability.

known_defects.title: A Requirement cannot express a date range, so historical questions about a named period are silently answered with the most recent window
known_defects.detail: MCP's get_rate_history accepts start_date and end_date, but Requirement carries only `rows`. McpAgent._history always asks the provider for the default window (the last calendar year) and takes the N most recent rows. A question about 2008 is therefore answered with 2025-2026 data. The row shortfall is reported honestly; the date substitution is not.
known_defects.fix: Requirement gained TemporalScope (as_of_date / start_date / end_date / lookback_days). It is derived by the domain expert, assessed by the MCP agent against real coverage, and passed into get_curve and get_rate_history. A period outside coverage is refused with out_of_range rather than silently replaced by the latest window. Enforced by test_a_named_historical_period_is_served_or_refused_never_substituted.

questions.question: Give me a year of 10-year yield history.
Give me 5,000 rows of 10-year yield history.
questions.intent: more than the agent path can deliver
questions.reason: PostgreSQL holds ~9,158 observations per par tenor, but the agent's history path reads the provider's default one-year window and caps at ~251 rows. The shortfall is reported honestly rather than padded.

questions.question: What was the 10-year yield during 2008?
questions.intent: history for a named past period
questions.reason: Served for the named period: TemporalScope carries the dates through the negotiation into get_rate_history.

questions.question: What was the 30-year yield on 1995-06-15?
questions.reason: Served for the named period: TemporalScope carries the dates through the negotiation into get_rate_history.

questions.question: Compare the 2-year and 10-year yields.
questions.reason: Both tenors arrive as columns of one table, so a reader can compare them; the difference is not computed by the system.

questions.question: How does the real 10-year yield compare with the nominal 10-year?
questions.reason: curve_family is a single value on the Requirement, so one answer carries one family. Both series exist in PostgreSQL; the agent cannot combine them, and combining a nominal par yield with a real yield on one curve is exactly what the quoting-basis rule forbids doing implicitly.

questions.question: Which tenor moved the most over the last year?
questions.reason: No aggregation or ranking exists in the agent path; the table is returned unreduced.

questions.question: What is the average 10-year yield over the last year?
questions.reason: There is no aggregation capability. McpAgent.execute returns a snapshot or a history table; no mean, min, max, percentile or volatility is computed anywhere in the agent path, and no MCP tool offers one.

questions.question: What is the highest 30-year yield ever recorded?
questions.reason: No aggregation capability, and no full-history access from the agent path (DEF-002).

questions.question: What is the realised volatility of the 10-year yield?
questions.reason: No volatility tool. The risk engine computes VaR/ES by historical simulation, which is a different quantity and is portfolio-scoped, not series-scoped.

questions.question: Is the yield curve currently inverted?
questions.intent: curve shape read from a snapshot
questions.reason: The full curve snapshot is returned and the knowledge base defines inversion, so the orchestrator can describe the shape from real numbers; no inversion flag is computed.

questions.question: What is the current 2s10s slope?
questions.intent: spread between two tenors in basis points
questions.reason: Both tenors are returned as a table and the spread is readable from it, but no schedulable capability computes the slope as a single value; get_curve_slope is correctly advertised as informational, so it is no longer named as a calculation and no longer fails at execution.

questions.question: Has the curve steepened or flattened recently?
questions.reason: Both tenors are returned as a table and the spread is readable from it, but no schedulable capability computes the slope as a single value; get_curve_slope is correctly advertised as informational, so it is no longer named as a calculation and no longer fails at execution.

questions.question: What is the DV01 of our equity book?
questions.intent: an asset class that does not exist here
questions.reason: Only one synthetic Treasury book exists (TREASURY_DEMO_001, five fixed-rate bonds). There is no equity data and DV01 is not an equity measure.

questions.question: Show me EUR/USD FX rates.
questions.intent: an asset class outside the datasets
questions.reason: All five datasets are U.S. Treasury interest rates. No FX series exists.

questions.question: Give me the CUSIP and issuer name for every bond in the 10-year sector.
questions.reason: A par yield curve holds no instrument records. treasury.bill_security does carry CUSIPs for bills, but it is not exposed through any MCP tool or agent path, and it does not cover the 10-year sector.

questions.question: What is our Basel capital ratio?
questions.intent: regulatory capital, known to the corpus only
questions.reason: No capital, RWA or balance-sheet data exists. The corpus covers it (regulatory_capital/basel_capital_ratios), so the system explains and declines.

questions.question: What is the 15-year Treasury yield?
questions.intent: a tenor Treasury does not publish
questions.reason: Treasury publishes no 15-year par yield; the curve jumps 10y to 20y. Interpolating one would be inventing an observation.

questions.question: What is the implied volatility of the 10-year option?
questions.reason: No options, no volatility surface, no pricing model for them.

questions.question: What was the 10-year yield on 1985-01-01?
questions.reason: Coverage begins 1990-01-02. Also blocked by DEF-002 (no date range on the Requirement).

questions.question: What was the 10-year yield on 2030-01-01?
questions.reason: Latest observation is 2026-08-11. The system must not forecast.

questions.question: Price the portfolio NOT_A_BOOK.
questions.reason: Only TREASURY_DEMO_001 exists. The MCP agent resolves the first available book rather than accepting an arbitrary id, so an unknown id cannot reach the risk engine.

questions.question: Compute VaR at 150% confidence.
questions.intent: a parameter outside its meaningful range
questions.reason: The requirement guard drops a confidence level outside (0,1) and records a warning, so the data layer's documented default stands rather than a nonsense parameter being used.
